Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — germanium: a brittle, lustrous grey-white semimetal predicted in 1871 as eka-silicon, with its weight, density, grey colour and even a chloride boiling below 100 degrees written down before anyone had seen it; found in 1886 when a silver ore from a Saxon mine called the Prince of Heaven kept weighing seven percent more than its silver and sulphur, every forecast number nearly right, and named for Germania; opaque to visible light yet clear to infrared, it makes the dark mirror-like lenses of heat cameras; in 1947 a small slab of germanium touched by two gold contacts became the first transistor; it dopes the cores of optical fibres — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.
